PID controllers

Source: R/pid.R
ctrl_pid.Rd

Define a PID controller with the features needed in practice: derivative filtering, setpoint weighting, output saturation, anti-windup and bumpless transfer. The control law (parallel form) is $$u = k_p (b\,r - y) + k_i \int (r - y)\,dt + k_d \frac{d}{dt} (c\,r - y)_f,$$ where the derivative acts on the filtered signal \((c r - y)_f = (c r - y) / (T_f s + 1)\) and b, c are setpoint weights (c = 0 avoids derivative kicks on setpoint steps). With form = "standard" the gains are given as \(k_p\), \(T_i\) and \(T_d\) with \(k_i = k_p / T_i\) and \(k_d = k_p T_d\).

Usage

ctrl_pid(
  kp = 1,
  ki = 0,
  kd = 0,
  Tf = NULL,
  derivative_filter = NULL,
  b = 1,
  c = 0,
  u_min = -Inf,
  u_max = Inf,
  antiwindup = c("backcalc", "clamp", "none"),
  kt = NULL,
  form = c("parallel", "standard"),
  dt = NULL,
  integral_method = c("forward", "backward", "tustin")
)

Arguments

kp

Proportional gain.

ki

Integral gain (parallel form) or integral time Ti (standard form; Inf disables integral action).

kd

Derivative gain (parallel form) or derivative time Td (standard form).

Tf

Derivative filter time constant.

derivative_filter

Alternative to Tf: the ratio N with Tf = Td / N.

b, c

Setpoint weights for the proportional and derivative terms.

u_min, u_max

Output saturation limits.

antiwindup

"backcalc", "clamp" or "none".

kt

Back-calculation tracking gain.

form

"parallel" or "standard".

dt

Sample interval of the discrete implementation (NULL for a continuous description; required for simulation).

integral_method

Discretization of the integral term.

Value

An object of class c("ctrl_pid", "ctrl_controller").

Details

The derivative filter time constant Tf is required whenever \(k_d \ne 0\): an unfiltered derivative is improper and amplifies measurement noise without bound. A common choice is \(T_f = T_d / N\) with \(N\) between 2 and 20 (derivative_filter = N).

Discrete implementation (used by ctrl_simulate_pid() and ctrl_pid_update()) with sample interval dt: backward Euler for the derivative filter, forward Euler for the integral by default (integral_method = "forward"; "backward" and "tustin" are also available), and saturation to [u_min, u_max]. Anti-windup options: "backcalc" (back-calculation, the integrator is driven by \(k_t (u_{sat} - u)\) with tracking gain kt, default \(1/\sqrt{T_i T_d}\) or \(1/T_i\)), "clamp" (conditional integration: the integrator is frozen while saturated in the direction of the error) or "none". Bumpless transfer from manual to automatic mode initializes the integrator so that the first automatic output equals the last manual output.

See also

ctrl_pid_tf(), ctrl_simulate_pid(), ctrl_pid_tune()

Examples

pid <- ctrl_pid(kp = 2, ki = 1, kd = 0.5, derivative_filter = 10,
                u_min = -1, u_max = 1, dt = 0.01)
pid
#> PID controller (discrete, dt = 0.01)
#>   kp = 2, ki = 1, kd = 0.5, Tf = 0.025
#>   setpoint weights b = 1, c = 0
#>   saturation [-1, 1], anti-windup: backcalc
ctrl_pid_tf(pid)
#> Transfer function (discrete time, dt = 0.01)
#> 
#>   16.29 z^2 - 31.99 z + 15.71
#>   ---------------------------
#>     z^2 - 1.714 z + 0.7143
